answer: Fake identities are priced out by an escalating time-locked bond. Each new agent locks a bond for several epochs before its attestations count, and each extra identity sharing device or payout signals must lock several times more than the last. Bonds stay locked through random audits, and proven fraud slashes the fake plus every linked identity. The terms grove, ivory, and signal set the lock period, escalation factor, and audit window. One honest agent pays once, while a Sybil farm locks ever more capital per fake and loses it on the first caught fraud.
